 "Have Korea Make Our Shampoo," Walmart Comes Calling... Korean Shampoo a Hit in U.S., Exports Surge 83%
 by Kwon Jaehee 
 Published 17 Nov.2026 08:58(KST) 
 Updated 17 Nov.2026 09:20(KST) 
 open/close 
 Share 
 Language 
 Text Size 
 Print 
 Walmart Purchasing Team to Visit Korea on November 18
KOTRA to Hold Private-Label Sourcing Consultation
K-Beauty Expands Beyond Skincare into Haircare
 View original image 
 Walmart, the largest retailer in the United States, is looking for Korean manufacturers to produce private-label (PB) cosmetics. As K-beauty gains popularity beyond skincare and expands into hair care, with exports of Korean shampoo to the U.S. surging by more than 80%, major local retailers have begun showing interest in the manufacturing capabilities of Korean companies. Attention is now focused on whether Korea's cosmetics industry will expand its presence in the U.S. beyond exports under its own brands and become part of global retailers' PB supply chains.
 According to industry sources on November 17, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) will hold a Walmart PB sourcing consultation event at its headquarters in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on November 18. The event was organized to explore potential partnerships with Korean beauty and personal care manufacturers in conjunction with a visit by Walmart's purchasing team. KOTRA accepted applications from around five Korean manufacturers from November 4 to 11.
 View original image 
 Walmart is interested in products including hair care, body care, and lotions. Eligible participants are companies capable of supplying PB products to the U.S. market or producing them through original equipment manufacturing (OEM) or original design manufacturing (ODM). Applicants were required to have English-language company and product materials and products registered with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
 According to export and import trade statistics from the Korea Customs Service, Korea's shampoo exports totaled $179.57 million from January to September this year, up 39% from the same period last year. In just nine months, exports had already surpassed the full-year total of $178.07 million in 2025. Growth in the U.S. market has been particularly pronounced. During the same period, Korean shampoo exports to the U.S. reached $40.85 million, a sharp 83.1% increase from a year earlier. The U.S. overtook China to become the largest export market for Korean shampoo. K-beauty's export portfolio, which has grown primarily on the strength of skincare, is now expanding to include scalp and hair care products.
 Growth in the U.S. hair care market is also evident locally. According to market research firm Circana, hair care sales at U.S. premium retail channels rose 11% in the first half of this year from a year earlier. Sales of hair serums in particular increased by about 60%.
 View original image 
 The hair care market is growing in part because consumer trends are shifting toward treating the scalp and hair like skin. Once centered on shampoo and conditioner, the hair care market has recently expanded into specialized care, with consumers using serums, tonics, and essences based on scalp conditions and hair concerns. Demand for premium products is also rising as the "skinification" trend spreads, encouraging consumers to choose functional products for their scalp and hair just as they select cosmetics for their facial skin. This shift in consumer behavior is creating new market opportunities for K-beauty companies that have traditionally grown through skincare. 
 "Skinification, the trend of treating the scalp and hair like skin, has recently been gaining traction worldwide," said Jeong Jiyoon, a researcher at NH Investment & Securities. "Hair care products account for only 4% of cosmetics exports, making them a category with significant growth potential. In 2027, growth in hair care product exports is expected to outpace the overall export growth rate."
 Korean beauty companies are also stepping up efforts to expand their hair care businesses with the U.S. market in mind. Amorepacific is targeting North America with brands including Mise-en-scène, Ryo, and LABO-H. It is expanding its product range to include scalp essences and hair oils, taking into account the diverse hair types and care habits of local consumers. Amorepacific has set a target of generating 1 trillion won in hair care revenue and achieving an overseas revenue share of more than 60% in the fiscal year running from July 2029 to June 2030.
 LG Household & Health Care is also expanding its sales network in the U.S. through its hair care brand Dr. Groot. A key feature of its strategy is offering product lines exclusively for North American consumers that are not sold in Korea. Its range centers on products such as shampoo, treatment, and scalp serum. In August, the brand entered 424 Sephora stores across the U.S.

 It remains uncertain whether the consultation event will lead to actual supply contracts. Walmart has not disclosed details such as order volumes, supply prices, or whether it has selected suppliers. "We cannot disclose the names of the Korean cosmetics manufacturers participating in the consultation, in consideration of requests from the companies," a KOTRA official said. "Through this event, we plan to explore the possibility of future cooperation on PB product supplies."
